Subject: Serious degradation in production after last-night model update

Evelyn,

We just saw a substantial production impact after the model update you rolled to our environment last night (model v2.1 with quant profile 'q4_neo'). Key symptoms:
- p99 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~820ms across endpoints since 02:00 UTC.
- Error rate climbed to ~4.1% (previously <0.2%).
- Sustained throughput dropped ~25% for our 128-token typical requests.

This is impacting user-facing features in our app and customers are complaining. I've attached a perf snapshot and a short trace. Please advise immediate rollback or an emergency hotfix — we need action within the hour.

Contracts is cc'd; they're already asking about SLA credit/impact. We are prepared to join a call right now.

Sanjay Patel

Folks — quick technical readout from an initial triage:
- Symptoms line up with an inefficient kernel path triggered by the new quant profile 'q4_neo' on the customer's GPU family (OrionThera is on NVIDIA A10G-class instances). For certain short-context requests our runtime is hitting a fallback kernel that increases per-token latency.
- Error rate appears correlated with failed runtime allocations at the peak; we see transient OOM/alloc-failure logs during batching spikes.
- Throughput drop is consistent with both the slower kernel and reduced batching efficiency.

Immediate mitigation steps I recommend (we can enact within ~30–45 mins):
A) Canary rollback: switch OrionThera traffic back to the prior quant profile (q2_8) for the v2.0 variant and observe for 30 mins.
B) If canary looks good, perform full rollback for their shard and restore autoscaling headroom to avoid allocation failures.
C) Collect full trace and kernel perf dump for a deeper offline fix (probable kernel selection/quant path bug).

I'm attaching a short trace excerpt. I'll be on the call in 10.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Aditya — quick exec summary and asks following yesterday's Sev1 with OrionThera (DEAL-4982). Context: a model variant update (v2.1 + quant profile q4_neo) caused p99 latency spike (~220ms -> ~820ms), error-rate to increase (~0.2% -> 4.1%), and throughput to drop ~25% for OrionThera.

What we did:
- Canary rollback to prior quant profile (q2_8) at 08:55 on Nov 26; full rollback completed by 09:40. Post-rollback metrics returned to baseline within 20 minutes.
- Engineering captured kernel traces and root-cause analysis points to quant profile triggering a fallback kernel on customer GPU family.
- CS provided immediate MAP and draft goodwill credit to customer; legal/contracts are engaged.

Customer impact: production features degraded for ~1 hour; customer support tickets and a push from their contracts team for a commercial remedy.

Asks / decisions for execs:
1) Approve the proposed goodwill credit of 3% on the current invoice for immediate customer remediation.
2) Approve prioritization of a kernel/quant-path patch for our runtime — estimated engineering effort: 2 sprints (backlog PR opened).
3) Greenlight a short-term dedicated capacity offer (discounted month) for OrionThera while we complete the fix — product team to draft offer.

Related artifacts: mutual action plan draft and perf traces here: https://drive.redwood.internal/orionthera/mutual_action_plan_4982

I recommend a short exec sync at 17:00 to sign off on the commercial ask and outreach script.
